title: Refactor Git hooks into a single dispatcher architecture
objective: Replace the split Git hook installers with scripts/git_hooks.mjs, a uniform dispatch-based hook body, and one named function for every Git hook documented by the supported Git githooks manual while preserving existing SDLC validation, branch, merge, tag, and push behavior.

branch.name: WI-0031-git-hook-dispatcher
branch.rationale: The hook architecture refactor must be planned on main and processed on a dedicated context branch.

request.text: Prepare a new .docs/work-items/* to refactor Git hook installation around one scripts/git_hooks.mjs dispatcher with one function per unique hook name. Every installed hook must have the same thin dispatch body. Remove install_sdlc_validate_git_hooks.mjs, preserve existing hook behavior through named dispatcher functions, update documentation and tests, then commit the work item.

scope.name: single-hook-dispatcher
scope.description: Create scripts/git_hooks.mjs as the only hook behavior dispatcher, exposing dispatch(args) and one named function for every Git hook documented by the supported Git githooks manual.
scope.reason: Hook behavior should be centralized and changed by updating one dispatcher module.

scope.name: uniform-installed-hook-body
scope.description: Install every documented Git hook with the same thin body that dispatches using the hook name and original arguments.
scope.reason: Installed hook files should not contain per-hook behavior or divergent wrapper logic.

scope.name: installer-consolidation
scope.description: Remove scripts/install_sdlc_validate_git_hooks.mjs and make scripts/install.mjs install the unified dispatcher.
scope.reason: Two overlapping installers currently own overlapping hook behavior.

scope.name: behavior-preserving-migration
scope.description: Preserve work-item validation, task-processing branch enforcement, post-merge reminders, deterministic pre-push release checks, and unmanaged hook content/idempotence.
scope.reason: The refactor is architectural and should not silently change enforcement semantics.

nonGoals.name: hook-policy-expansion
nonGoals.description: Do not add new Git policy behavior beyond the existing branch, validation, completion, tag, and push rules.
nonGoals.reason: This work item is a dispatcher architecture refactor.

nonGoals.name: remote-server-enforcement
nonGoals.description: Do not claim Git server-side enforcement from local hook dispatch.

nonGoals.name: release-version-bump
nonGoals.description: Do not release a package version as part of the architecture refactor unless a separate delivery task requires it.
nonGoals.reason: The request is for a work item and architecture plan, not an implementation release.

items.name: dispatcher-contract
items.description: scripts/git_hooks.mjs must expose dispatch(args) and one uniquely named function for every Git hook documented by the supported Git githooks manual, with dispatch selecting the function from the hook name argument.
items.reason: The implementation needs one clear behavior ownership boundary.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The dispatcher listing contains every documented Git hook, dispatching each listed hook calls its named function, and unknown hook names return an actionable non-zero error.
The dispatcher preserves Git hook arguments and stdin for hooks such as pre-push.

items.name: uniform-hook-body
items.description: Every installed documented Git hook must contain the same thin executable body that calls scripts/git_hooks.mjs dispatch with the hook name and original arguments.
items.reason: Hook files should be stable wrappers rather than duplicated policy implementations.

acceptanceCriteria.description: All documented Git hook files have byte-equivalent dispatch bodies except for the hook-name argument, and the installer derives its complete file list from scripts/git_hooks.mjs.
Repeated installation is idempotent and unmanaged hook content is preserved.

items.name: installer-removal
items.description: scripts/install_sdlc_validate_git_hooks.mjs must be removed and scripts/install.mjs must be the only installer for the unified dispatcher.
items.reason: The current two-installer split causes overlapping ownership and confusing managed markers.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The old installer is absent, no installed hook references it, and --hooks installs the unified dispatch wrappers for every documented Git hook.

items.name: behavior-preservation
items.description: Existing work-item validation, branch processing, post-merge, pre-push release, no-remote, and failure-output behavior remains covered at the dispatcher boundary.
items.reason: The refactor must not weaken or change existing SDLC enforcement.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The complete hook and CLI test suite passes, including dispatcher routing and representative each-hook behavior.
The repository guidance and external SDLC SKILL.md document the unified dispatcher architecture and installation command.

items.name: work-item-traceability
items.description: The implementation, validation, and architecture documentation remain separately traceable through task envelopes.
items.reason: The repository requires task-level implementation and validation evidence.

acceptanceCriteria.description: WI-0031 task artifacts validate with zero invalid objects and zero unresolved references.

versionSuggestion.rationale: Refactors local hook installation and dispatch without changing the intended SDLC enforcement behavior.
versionSuggestion.disclaimer: This is an inferred recommendation; increase the impact if final changes are larger or more breaking than expected.
